ideas.name: C1: Covariate-shift importance reweighting
ideas.description: Fit a logistic classifier (sklearn) distinguishing eastern training rows from the western unlabeled test covariates; use predicted odds as density-ratio weights in the absolute-loss fit, clipped to a robust cap. This reweights training rows toward the deployment region's covariate distribution, directly targeting the geographic shift that inflates MAE.

ideas.name: C2: Huber-quantile hybrid loss
ideas.description: Replace the absolute loss with a Huberized quantile loss at tau=0.5: quadratic for small residuals, linear beyond a cross-validated threshold, solved by scipy least_squares or IRLS. The bulk-calibrated credal set in LV mainly protects the tail; a Huber-quantile fit may achieve lower central MAE while retaining mild tail robustness under the western shift.

ideas.name: C3: Shrunk robust ensemble
ideas.description: Fit LV, plain LAD, and ridge on the training split; also fit LAD on reweighted rows. Average the three predictors with weights chosen by leave-one-out cross-validation on eastern absolute error, then shrink the ensemble coefficients toward the LAD fit by a CV-tuned factor. Combining complementary robust fits often reduces MAE beyond any single fit.
